anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both GND1 (pin 4) and GND2 (pin 5) connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: An isolated CAN transceiver must keep its logic-side ground (GND1) and bus-side ground (GND2) separate to preserve galvanic isolation; the specification describes isolated CAN buses.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The intended isolation between the CM4 logic ground and the CAN bus ground is defeated, creating ground loops and making CAN0/CAN1 non-isolated.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of D4, D14, and D23; it has no supply, driver, or other connection in the netlist.
anomalies.expected: A net named for switched 3.3 V LED power should connect to a 3.3 V supply or LED-power switch so that the LEDs can be powered; otherwise the LED indicators cannot operate.
anomalies.impact: D4, D14, and D23 have floating anodes and will not light, causing the associated status/Ethernet indicators to behave differently from the intended powered-LED design.

anomalies.observed: R34 is given as value "120k" and is simulated as 120k, while its description and MPN identify a 120 Ω resistor.
anomalies.expected: For CAN termination, the resistor should be 120 Ω; the matching CAN1 termination resistor R35 is correctly listed as 120R.

evidence.quote: (description " 100mW Thick Film Resistors 75V ±100ppm/℃ ±1% 120Ω 0603 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If assembled as 120 kΩ, CAN0 termination is ineffective, degrading CAN bus signal quality and communication reliability.

parsed.summary: The design files show at least one clear architectural anomaly: the isolated CAN transceivers U10/U11 have GND1 and GND2 merged into the same GND net, defeating the specified CAN isolation. A floating LED power net and a 120 kΩ CAN termination value mismatch are also supported by the files.
